intro.title: Status Card
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Status Card component that displays different status indicators with dynamic styling based on the current state. You'll learn how to create reusable Angular components that accept input properties and conditionally apply CSS classes to show various status types like success, warning, or error. The lesson covers core Angular concepts including component creation, property binding with @Input decorators, and conditional class binding using ngClass. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces to define status types, component templates for the HTML structure, and CSS styling to create visually distinct status indicators. By the end, you'll have a flexible status card that can be reused throughout an Angular application to communicate different states to users.
intro.usecase: Status cards are ubiquitous in modern web applications, appearing in dashboards to display system health, user activity, or performance metrics with color-coded indicators. They're commonly used in project management tools like Jira or Trello to show task status, in e-commerce admin panels to display order states, and in monitoring applications to indicate server uptime or alert conditions. Social media platforms use status cards to show user online/offline states, while enterprise software employs them for displaying approval workflows, document review states, or compliance statuses. As a developer, you'll frequently build these components to provide users with quick visual feedback about the current state of data or processes in your applications.
